subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a cross-channel Gateway receipt timestamp to agents, and if so what field name, trust block, and timestamp format should be the stable contract?
rationale: The missing field is source-proven, but the fix would create a durable agent-visible metadata and plugin SDK surface across channels, so automation should not choose the public contract unilaterally.

options.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
options.body: Expose a single cross-channel field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` in the chosen metadata block and carry it through SDK/channel ingress with tests for at least one durable and one direct path.

options.title: Keep timing in diagnostics only
options.body: Do not add agent-visible metadata and instead solve latency attribution through Gateway/channel stage logs or trace events.

options.title: Leave it to channel plugins
options.body: Let each plugin expose its own receipt timing, accepting inconsistent field names and weaker cross-channel comparability.

recommendation.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
recommendation.body: Expose a single cross-channel field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` in the chosen metadata block and carry it through SDK/channel ingress with tests for at least one durable and one direct path.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and verified the adjacent timestamp metadata PR and appear in recent checked-out history for the core prompt/envelope surface.
